newsitem.title: USA: Rural U.S. rebounding but unevenly-KC Fed's Hoenig.
newsitem.headline: Rural U.S. rebounding but unevenly-KC Fed's Hoenig.

text.p: The rural economy is rebounding and showing robust job growth, Thomas Hoenig, president of the Kansas City Federal Reserve Bank, said Thursday, but the gains have been uneven.
"Rural America is enjoying an economic rebound in the 1990s," Hoenig said at a conference, "Financing Rural America," sponsored by his bank.
The growth rate for jobs has been 1.5 percent a year, he said, and rural population has grown one percent this decade.

Hoenig and other speakers said economic development would require additional capital. During comments to open the conference, he said reductions in federal subsidies would add to the need for access to capital.
Rural economic gains have been uneven, he said. The areas that benefitted the most are those with scenic values or ready access from urban areas.
Demographers reported a "rural renaissance" in the 1970s as people moved back to rural areas after decades of migration to urban jobs. The recession of the mid-1980s stunted that trend.
A quarter of the U.S. population lives in rural areas.
